name: AMD Instinct GPU server solutions via AMD's OEM and system-builder partners
region: Worldwide; AMD publishes a qualified-server catalog PDF and a partner logo list
notes:
QUOTE-ONLY - AMD publishes no accelerator price list at all, so price_usd is null by evidence, not by omission. This is the best-documented OEM channel of the three accelerator vendors because AMD publishes the partner roster explicitly on the Instinct where-to-buy page: Advantech, AMAX, ASRock Rack, ASUS, Bull AI, CANCOM, Colfax Customized Solutions, Dell Technologies, Eviden, Exxact, GIGABYTE, HPE, Aivres, Inventec, KOI Computers, Lenovo, MiTAC, MSI, Nor-tech, PEGATRON, Penguin Solutions, Supermicro, Symmetric Computing, Wistron. That list is the practical answer to 'who can actually sell me an MI350X' - it is long, unlike NVIDIA's, and it is a real sourcing advantage for AMD. Featured systems AMD names directly: Dell PowerEdge XE9785/XE9785L (6U), HPE ProLiant Compute XD685 (6U, 5th Gen EPYC), GIGABYTE G893-ZX1 (8U), Supermicro AS-8126GS-TNMR (8U). AMD also runs a Helios rackscale solution (72x MI455X) as the flagship. BASIS: as with HGX, Instinct accelerators in these systems are OAM modules on the baseboard and arrive WITH the system - there is no retail single-OAM SKU from AMD, so any 'per-GPU MI350X price' is a derived allocation, never a list price. Access motion is 'Contact Sales' plus the OEM catalogue; cloud access is a separate route. EXPORT CONTROLLED (true). Regime: US BIS advanced-computing export controls (the Oct 2023 interim final rule, 88 FR 73458 - source sup-buy-bis-2023-advanced-computing-controls), which put datacenter accelerators under ECCN 3A090/4A090, added the advanced-computing Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rule, and extended Regional Stability (RS) controls to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5. For items destined to Macau or Country Group D:5 the rule applies a PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL; other RS destinations get a presumption of approval. Practical effect: which accelerator you can legally be sold, and which SKU counts as compliant, is set by destination and end user - not by the channel.

 LEAD TIME: null, deliberately. AMD publishes no lead time in weeks for Instinct MI300X/MI325X/MI350X on any page, and this channel is quote-only, so a number here would be invented. The honest comparison is with NVIDIA, whose primary filing does disclose the shape of its horizon ($95.2bn of purchase and supply/capacity obligations substantially payable through FY2027 - source spl-nvda-10k-fy2026-supply-commitments); a rival that publishes nothing at all is a procurement risk, not a shorter lead time, and the MI325X is the part BIS singled out by name in the January 2026 case-by-case rule (91 FR 1684), so its export path is documented while its delivery path is not.

 LEAD TIME: null and it is an EXPLICIT NEGATIVE, checked 2026-10-04. This is a quote-only channel - no price and no lead time is published on any page, and AGENTS.md forbids inventing an unsourced number, so the field stays null with the reason recorded. The negative is itself a procurement fact: a channel that will not state a lead time is a channel where the lead time is set by whatever allocation you happen to have, and it is exactly the kind of number to ask for in writing before signing. Probe log and per-vendor detail in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time; the one figure published anywhere in this chain is AWS's 8-week MAXIMUM Capacity Block booking horizon, which is a commitment ceiling rather than a delivery time.
